orgs.label: STXBP1 Foundation
orgs.summary: US parent-led foundation for STXBP1-related disorders. Runs a grants program, supports the STARR natural history study and the S-COMB outcome-measure consortium, has a scientific advisory board and holds an annual STXBP1 Summit+.

evidence.quote: The STXBP1 Foundation is a non-profit advocacy organization dedicated to creating awareness and finding a cure for STXBP1 disorders.
The STXBP1 Foundation is a parent-led 501(c)3 non-profit

scientific_advisory_board.quote: Ingo Helbig, MD Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia John Oldenhof, MSc, PhD BioPharma Services Jose Rizo-Rey, PhD UT SouthWestern Medical Center Matthijs Verhage, PhD VU University Amsterdam

orgs.label: SLC6A1 Connect
orgs.summary: US parent-led advocacy group for SLC6A1-related disorders, founded in 2018. It points families to Simons Searchlight, Citizen Health and a COMBINEDBrain/Across Matrix natural history platform, collects biorepository samples with COMBINEDBrain and runs an international scientific symposium and family conference.

evidence.quote: SLC6A1 Connect is a parent-led patient advocacy organization dedicated to improving the lives of children and families affected by SLC6A1-related disorders.

orgs.label: The Baker-Gordon Syndrome Foundation
orgs.summary: Family foundation for Baker-Gordon syndrome (SYT1-associated neurodevelopmental disorder). It keeps a family registry and invites families to the first natural history study, run by the University of Missouri.

evidence.quote: The Baker-Gordon Syndrome Foundation was founded to help families affected by this syndrome make connections with one another.
Baker-Gordon Syndrome (BAGOS), also known as, SYT1-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (SYT1 Syndrome) is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the Synaptotagmin-1 (SYT1) gene.
The Baker Gordon Syndrome Foundation , USA

orgs.label: Snap25 Foundation
orgs.summary: Parent-run foundation for SNAP25 disorders. It runs a SNAP25 Data Collection Program on the RARE-X platform and has a scientific advisory board.

evidence.quote: Snap25 Foundation's mission is: Research to accelerate research to cure Snap25 disorders
Donations are tax-deductible in the US.
New York, NY, USA
We are dedicated to raising awareness of the genetic disorder caused by mutations in the gene SNAP25, and working towards finding a cure.

scientific_advisory_board.quote: Dedicated to raising awareness of the genetic disorder caused by mutations in the gene Snap25, and working towards finding a cure.

orgs.label: VAMP2.org / Raging Raymond Foundation
orgs.summary: Family-founded VAMP2 community site, linked to the Raging Raymond Foundation, with a scientific advisory board page and research updates. It reports an MRC-funded UCL–Yale project on VAMP2 disorders.

evidence.quote: VAMP2 is now understood to cause neurodevelopmental disorders, such as visual impairments, movement disorders and epilepsy.
In 2018, the first case of a VAMP2 genetic variant was diagnosed in the United States.

Our mission is to spread awareness about rare genetic conditions impairing brain development and neurological development in children, advocate for the causes, drive research into the disorders, and seek therapeutic interventions.

orgs.summary: Nonprofit consortium led by patient advocacy groups. It shares research infrastructure (biorepository, PAG Matrix natural-history portals, EEG bank, outcome-measures library) across more than 130 rare neurological disorder communities, including SLC6A1 and STXBP1.

evidence.quote: COMBINEDBrain is a nonprofit consortium led by patient advocacy foundations and supported by clinicians, researchers, and pharmaceutical partners working to develop treatments for rare neurological disorders.

orgs.label: Muscular Dystrophy Association (MDA)
orgs.scope: umbrella: neuromuscular diseases incl. congenital myasthenic syndromes
orgs.summary: US neuromuscular umbrella organisation with a disease program for congenital myasthenic syndromes (CMS), including presynaptic forms. SYT2 causes a presynaptic CMS (CMS7, per NORD). MDA's page does not name SYT2.

evidence.quote: There are many types of CMS, grouped into three main categories named for the part of the neuromuscular junction that's affected: presynaptic (the nerve cell), postsynaptic (the muscle cell) or synaptic (the space in between).

SYT2.quote: There are many types of CMS, grouped into three main categories named for the part of the neuromuscular junction that's affected: presynaptic (the nerve cell), postsynaptic (the muscle cell) or synaptic (the space in between).
Any congenital myasthenic syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SYT2 gene.

assets.label: STARR (STXBP1 Clinical Trial Ready) natural history study
assets.access: Families enrol at 5 US clinical sites; data are intended for regulatory-grade outcome measures

evidence.quote: STARR stands for STXBP1 Clinical Trial Ready) and is a natural history study for STXBP1-Related Disorders (STXBP1-RD) developed to better understand how the disorder affects someone over time.
Currently, all 5 sites are enrolling participants with STXBP1-RD.
Dr. Ingo Helbig of CHOP leads the NHS for both STXBP1 and SYNGAP1.

assets.label: S-COMB: STXBP1 Clinical Outcome Measures & Biomarker Consortium
assets.access: Consortium of researchers, clinicians, advocates and pharma; guidance shared with STARR and ESCO natural history studies

evidence.quote: The S-COMB is a collaborative network of researchers, healthcare providers, advocates, pharmaceutical companies, and other STXBP1 stakeholders brought together to share knowledge on STXBP1 and discuss, develop, test, and validate a set of clinical and research assessments that can be used to facilitate therapeutic advancements and improve clinical outcomes in STXBP1 patients.

The Consortium will provide guidance and expert advice to the pre-competitive, prospective STARR natural history study being conducted in North America and the European STXBP1 Consoritum (ESCO) natural history study

assets.label: Floxed-null Stxbp1 mouse (InnoSer CRO)
assets.access: Commercial: in vivo efficacy testing offered by the CRO InnoSer (Belgium)

evidence.quote: Among the research models they offer is the floxed null Stxbp1 mouse maintained on a pure C57BL/6J genetic background.

This model demonstrates epileptic-like activity and muscle twitches as measured by EEG and EMG and robust cognitive impairment and behavioral disturbances, which have been demonstrated to respond to antiseizure medications.

assets.label: Stxbp1 haploinsufficient mouse models (Xue lab, Baylor / Texas Children's)
assets.access: Academic lab models; contact the Xue lab (Baylor College of Medicine)

evidence.quote: The Xue team generated two genetically distinct mutant mouse models in which STXBP1 protein levels were reduced by 50% in most brain regions.

assets.label: ENDD Center (Penn / CHOP): STXBP1 & SYNGAP1 therapeutics and shared models
assets.access: Cellular and mouse models to be shared with interested researchers

evidence.quote: To accomplish these goals ENDD is developing cellular and preclinical mouse models of STXBP1 and SYNGAP disorders, which will also be important resources for the research community and will readily be shared with interested parties.

assets.label: MRC-funded UCL–Yale VAMP2 / SNAREopathy research project
assets.access: Academic project; includes a mouse model carrying a human VAMP2 mutation

evidence.quote: We will also address the consequences for the function of small neuronal circuits in a mouse model carrying a human mutation.

The proposed research will provide much-needed clarity on the mechanisms of VAMP2 mutations, build towards a viable treatment option that can be translated to the clinic in due course, and define a research pipeline that can be applied to other SNAREopathies.
